findings.description: A major GitHub Actions update can modify the privileged auto-merge workflow and then be auto-merged.
findings.analysis: The auto-merge workflow itself consumes the App key. A Dependabot update to an action in that workflow could be eligible under the configured GitHub Actions major-update policy, merging a modified privileged workflow without a human review.
findings.recommendation: Require human review for Dependabot updates that modify the privileged auto-merge workflow, while retaining the agreed policy for other GitHub Actions updates.
findings.rationale: The project intentionally trusts GitHub-maintained actions, including major updates, when the required CI gate passes. This is not treated as a separate privileged-workflow exception.

findings.description: The App that enables auto-merge is a Main-ruleset bypass actor, which may permit a merge without Verify.
findings.analysis: This conflicts with the design requirement that auto-merge wait for Verify. The current ruleset intentionally grants the Uniquode App an always-bypass, so the delivery policy must choose whether that bypass remains compatible with auto-merge.
findings.recommendation: Accept: retain the trusted Uniquode App bypass, but revise the workflow so it inspects the target PR's required checks, including Verify, and invokes the App's merge capability only after they pass.
findings.rationale: The App bypass is intentional, but GitHub's later auto-merge gate is insufficient. The auto-merge workflow itself must establish that all required checks, including Verify, are passing before it invokes the trusted App's merge capability.

findings.description: Verify is not required by the Main ruleset.
findings.analysis: The live Main ruleset was updated before this review and now requires the Verify context; no old job contexts are required.
findings.recommendation: Decline as already addressed by the live repository configuration.
findings.rationale: Verified against the live active Main ruleset: Verify is its sole required status check, and PR #10 reports Verify as successful.

findings.description: The workflow uses the legacy app-id input for a Client ID variable.
findings.analysis: The action accepts app-id as a legacy alias, so the workflow is not broken. Its current documentation recommends the explicit client-id input, which matches the configured variable name.
findings.recommendation: Decline: retain app-id because the configured value is the GitHub App ID.
findings.rationale: The current v3 action manifest explicitly supports app-id as the GitHub App ID. The configured value is an App ID, despite the repository variable's historical CLIENT_ID name.

findings.description: A Dependabot-triggered workflow cannot access the App private key.
findings.analysis: The workflow uses pull_request_target. GitHub's Dependabot restriction applies to that event only when Dependabot created the base ref; this project targets its human-owned main branch. The configured repository secret is therefore available in the intended case.
findings.recommendation: Configure AUTOMERGE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY as a Dependabot secret.
findings.rationale: GitHub documents Dependabot secrets as the secret store for workflows initiated by Dependabot. The required secret has now been configured there by the user.

findings.description: An eligibility decision can race with a newer Dependabot head update.
findings.analysis: The workflow evaluates metadata and enables auto-merge by pull-request URL rather than an immutable head SHA. A newer update can arrive between those operations.
findings.recommendation: Determine whether GitHub clears auto-merge on Dependabot pushes; if it does not, bind the action to the inspected head and cancel stale runs.
findings.rationale: This is disproportionate race hardening for the intended Dependabot automation. Dependabot updates are expected before merge, and the normal required-check flow handles the current revision.

findings.description: An ineligible later update may retain previously enabled auto-merge.
findings.analysis: The workflow does not disable a prior auto-merge setting when a later run is ineligible. This overlaps the head-update race and depends on GitHub's behaviour when Dependabot updates a branch.
findings.recommendation: Handle with the stale-eligibility finding after confirming GitHub's automatic reset behaviour.
findings.rationale: This depends on the same speculative stale-head scenario as item 6. In the intended flow, an eligible pull request passes required checks and is merged; it cannot later become ineligible.

findings.analysis: Repository settings were updated before the review. GitHub now reports allow_auto_merge: true.
findings.recommendation: Decline as already addressed by the live repository configuration.
findings.rationale: Verified against the live repository setting: allow_auto_merge is true.
